requirements.text: Resolve schedules into stable run IDs and bound pending work per origin.
Deduplicate source revisions while retaining fetch provenance and parser version.
Recover partial runs without advancing progress past committed outputs.

problem.scope: Extend the synthetic collection exercise with scheduled run identity, origin politeness, deduplication and provenance. Inputs are authored URLs and synthetic records; no live crawler or extraction is claimed.

provenance.note: Authored interview preparation. Technical references support mechanisms, not the claim that a company asked this question.

references.supports: Transactions isolate concurrent authorization and mutation decisions; retries remain explicit.

references.supports: Robots policy governs crawler access; authorization and per-origin rate policy are separate.
references.title: Robots protocol

acceptanceCases.given: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement.
acceptanceCases.then: Retain one accepted output and the original provenance.
acceptanceCases.when: Retry the same source revision under a new lease.

acceptanceCases.given: A parser rejects one fetched record.
acceptanceCases.then: Keep the invalid receipt quarantined and never report it committed.

acceptanceCases.given: The scheduler fires the same tick twice and one origin has more URLs than its pending bound.
acceptanceCases.then: Both triggers return one runId; that origin holds only its bound of pending leases while the rest wait.
acceptanceCases.when: Create the run and fill the frontier.

evidence.testName: L024 frontier output commit is lease-fenced and deduplicated by source revision and parser

acceptanceCases.given: Source S revision r1 is leased at epoch 1; its worker commits but loses the acknowledgement, and one record fails parsing.
acceptanceCases.then: The retry returns duplicate with the original provenance; the stale worker is rejected and marks nothing done; the invalid record stays quarantined once and out of the output.
acceptanceCases.when: Reassign the lease to epoch 2 and retry r1; then let the epoch-1 worker commit revision r2 late.

guarantees: Retries consume the same per-origin budget.
A timeout is retryable intent, not evidence of an empty source.
Invalid records never enter the accepted output table.
The completion marker never outruns output commit.
A stale worker cannot complete a reassigned lease.
A record is attributable to immutable inputs.

solutions.chooseWhen: Sources expose stable URLs and incremental crawl latency is acceptable.

stages.explanation: Resolve schedules into stable run IDs and bound pending work per origin. A (scheduleId, scheduledFor) pair creates at most one run, and pending leases per origin never exceed the configured bound. [A directed acyclic graph](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Directed_acyclic_graph) expresses work that depends on earlier results. A scheduler must track completed dependencies and distinguish logical tasks from retry attempts before releasing downstream work.
invariants: A (scheduleId, scheduledFor) pair creates at most one run, and pending leases per origin never exceed the configured bound.
stages.question: How does one schedule tick become one stable run with bounded per-origin pending work?
stages.reason: Resolve schedules into stable run IDs and bound pending work per origin.
stages.title: Define the operation boundary

stages.explanation: Create one run per schedule/instant and admit only configured origins. Own normalized URL/revision keys, lease owner, attempts and next eligible time. Lease owner, epoch, attempts and next eligible time live only in the frontier; a worker's claim is valid only for the current lease epoch. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources. A newer owner needs a token that the resource checks, not merely a belief that ownership changed.
invariants: Lease owner, epoch, attempts and next eligible time live only in the frontier; a worker's claim is valid only for the current lease epoch.
stages.question: Who owns URL leases, attempts and next-eligible times?
stages.reason: Create one run per schedule/instant and admit only configured origins. Own normalized URL/revision keys, lease owner, attempts and next eligible time.
stages.title: Expose authority and state

stages.explanation: Grant a bounded concurrent permit after robots and minimum-delay checks. Retries consume the same per-origin budget. [A content delivery network](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Content_delivery_network) serves reusable content near viewers. Cache keys, freshness rules, and origin fallback determine whether that improves latency without serving the wrong version. Consider this case: The scheduler fires the same tick twice and one origin has more URLs than its pending bound.
invariants: Retries consume the same per-origin budget.

operations.reason: Expose this new typed path without mutating earlier binding definitions.

stages.question: How is one busy site protected?
stages.reason: Grant a bounded concurrent permit after robots and minimum-delay checks.
stages.title: Origin permit

stages.explanation: Use finite response-size/time limits and conditional validators; retain status and receipt. A timeout is retryable intent, not evidence of an empty source. [A condition variable](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Condition_variable) lets a thread sleep until shared state may have changed. Waking does not guarantee success, so the protected condition must be checked again. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement.
invariants: A timeout is retryable intent, not evidence of an empty source.
stages.question: What if a fetch times out?
stages.reason: Use finite response-size/time limits and conditional validators; retain status and receipt.
stages.title: Fetch executor

stages.explanation: Parse retained bytes with a pinned parser version and emit schema errors to quarantine. Invalid records never enter the accepted output table. [Data ingestion](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Data_integration) moves source records into a usable destination. Stable source identity and progress records distinguish genuinely new data from repeated delivery or a restarted import. Consider this case: A parser rejects one fetched record. Finish the bounded run.
invariants: Invalid records never enter the accepted output table.
stages.question: Can a new parser reinterpret old content?
stages.reason: Parse retained bytes with a pinned parser version and emit schema errors to quarantine.
stages.title: Versioned parser

stages.explanation: Under the current lease epoch, commit unique source/revision/parser outputs, quarantined rejects and the completion marker atomically; an existing output returns duplicate with its original provenance. The completion marker never outruns output commit. [Transaction guarantees](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ACID) describe which changes become visible together and what survives failure. They must be tied to explicit storage behavior rather than inferred from a successful API call.
invariants: The completion marker never outruns output commit.
stages.question: When may the frontier advance?
stages.reason: Under the current lease epoch, commit unique source/revision/parser outputs, quarantined rejects and the completion marker atomically; an existing output returns duplicate with its original provenance.
stages.title: Output transaction

stages.explanation: Fence expired lease holders and retry with the same run/revision identity. A stale worker cannot complete a reassigned lease. [Fencing](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fencing_%28computing%29) prevents an outdated owner from continuing to modify shared resources. A newer owner needs a token that the resource checks, not merely a belief that ownership changed. Consider this case: Source S revision r1 is leased at epoch 1; its worker commits but loses the acknowledgement, and one record fails parsing.
invariants: A stale worker cannot complete a reassigned lease.

operations.reason: Expose this new typed path without mutating earlier binding definitions.

stages.question: What if a worker dies mid-fetch?
stages.reason: Fence expired lease holders and retry with the same run/revision identity.
stages.title: Lease recovery

stages.explanation: Retain source URL, receipt hash, parser version, scheduled instant and terminal state. A record is attributable to immutable inputs. [Replication](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Replication_%28computing%29) keeps copies of state on multiple nodes. Copying data alone does not decide which copy may accept writes or how much stale data a read may return. Consider this case: A worker commits output but loses its acknowledgement.
invariants: A record is attributable to immutable inputs.
stages.question: How is one record explained?
stages.reason: Retain source URL, receipt hash, parser version, scheduled instant and terminal state.
stages.title: Provenance index

tradeoffs: Frontier leases and per-origin queues add state.
Content changes need revision-aware deduplication rather than URL-only suppression.

acceptanceCases.given: A partition output is complete but a worker restarts.
One manifest partition is quarantined or missing.
acceptanceCases.then: Refuse pointer swap and retain the prior generation.

acceptanceCases.given: Two triggers for the same scheduledFor arrive, the second after a source changed.
acceptanceCases.then: The first freeze wins; the second trigger returns the same runId and manifestHash instead of freezing a new snapshot.

acceptanceCases.given: A failed run left staging output while generation 3 is active.
acceptanceCases.then: Abandoned staging is deleted; generation 3 and its provenance are kept.
acceptanceCases.when: Run the retention planner after lease expiry and the retention period.

evidence.testName: L024 manifest publication compares and swaps the prior generation and refuses older runs

acceptanceCases.given: Generation 1 is active; run 3, a slower run 2 and run 4 all started while 1 was active, and run 3 first has one quarantined partition.
acceptanceCases.then: Run 3 publishes only when complete; runs 2 and 4 fail the compare-and-swap; run 2 then fails the newer-generation check while run 4 publishes, so the pointer never moves backward.
acceptanceCases.when: Publish run 3 before and after its last receipt commits; publish runs 2 and 4 expecting 1; then publish run 2 and run 4 expecting 3.

guarantees: Ranges are disjoint and cover exactly the frozen manifest.
A reassignment retains the same partition identity.
Quarantine counts remain visible in run completeness.
Readers cannot confuse staging rows with the published snapshot.
Only a complete run publishes, by compare-and-swap from the generation it expected to a strictly newer one; a late older run never rolls the pointer back.
Cleanup never deletes the active generation.
